svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Traditional app vs. Mojito, an evolving app
svg.desc: Left: a traditional app, a UI on top of a large hard-coded backend of services, rules and pipelines; every change waits for the next release. Right: Mojito, the same UI on a thin hub on your server. On your Mac (or a Mac mini) an agent, Claude Code, can read your context (mail, calendar, files, logins) and the app's own code and design. You ask in plain words, for example "Put the next step on top, in bold.", and the agent rewrites the app; changes it judges risky wait for your OK.
svg.text: Frozen code: someone else decides what it does.
Every change waits for the next release.
Thin code: an agent with your context changes the app itself.
Hub on your server: storage, API, push
it knows how it is built
You: “Put the next step on top, in bold.”
